title: census.py run and finish commit every tracked change under the root, not only what their steps wrote
goal: census.py run and finish commit only the census logs and the paths their steps wrote, so an operator's uncommitted article edit made before the run is never swept into the phase-1 or the confirmed-dates commit

run:
import os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, '_tools')
import census, kbcommon
d = tempfile.mkdtemp()
G = lambda *a: subprocess.run(['git', '-C', d, *a], capture_output=True, text=True)
G('init', '-q'); G('config', 'user.email', 't@example.com'); G('config', 'user.name', 't')
os.makedirs(d + '/kb/public/_census')
for f in ('a.md', 'b.md'):
    open(d + '/kb/public/' + f, 'w').write('base\n')
G('add', '.'); G('commit', '-qm', 'base')
open(d + '/kb/public/a.md', 'w').write('operator edit made before the run\n')
kbcommon.HOME = d
steps = [{'name': 'write', 'argv': ['python3', '-c', "open('kb/public/b.md', 'w').write('step\\n')"], 'ok': (0,), 'skip': '', 'capture': False},
         {'name': 'commit', 'argv': ['git', 'commit', '-m', 'census'], 'ok': (0,), 'skip': '', 'capture': False, 'add': []}]
code, _ = census.drive(steps, 'kb/public', False, False, 'rerun')
got = G('show', '--name-only', '--format=', 'HEAD').stdout.split()
print('exit', code, 'committed', got)
sys.exit(0 if code == 0 and 'kb/public/b.md' in got and 'kb/public/a.md' not in got else 1)

gates.question: How does the commit step tell the paths a run's steps wrote from changes made before it? Snapshot plus kept record, snapshot only, or refuse any change under the root?
options: refuse any change under the root
